title: Ledger of Pellan Corvesso
author: Pellan Corvesso, Factor
pages: Fairday, Reaping. Grain at the quay four pence the bushel, cheapest this year. Bought two hundred. Wax candles from the Combes eight pence the dozen. Salt fish holds at a penny the fish.
Fairday, Leaffall. Grain five pence. Candles nine. A Combes waggoner says bandits on the Honey Lane took three carts. Bought every candle in the market. Mark my words.
Fairday, Dimming. Candles fifteen pence the dozen! Widows weeping at the stalls, cannot light their graves. Sold half. Kept half. The Tide-Wife looked at me as though I were a wrecker.
Fairday, Deepnight. Grain eleven pence. Blight in the Vale, they say, grey ears. Refugees at the gate. A kind stranger has opened a soup kitchen by the old chapel. Asks no fee. Strange.
Moot-day, Deepnight. The soup-stranger has fed two hundred. Some of those he fed now go out after the curfew bell. I have stopped selling him black candles. I should never have started.
